title: Alexander founds Alexandria in Arachosia
description: Alexander the Great founds a city on the site of Old Kandahar during his campaign through the eastern Achaemenid provinces.

title: Ashoka's Kandahar inscription
description: An edict of Ashoka is carved in Greek and Aramaic, showing Mauryan rule and the spread of Buddhist ideas in the region.

title: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom founded
description: The satrap Diodotus breaks away from the Seleucid Empire and founds a Greek kingdom in Bactria.

title: Buddhas of Bamiyan carved
description: Two giant standing Buddhas are cut into the cliff of the Bamiyan valley, a Buddhist centre on the trade routes between India and Central Asia.

title: Saffarids take Kabul
description: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth conquers Kabul from the Hindu Shahis, bringing Muslim rule to eastern Afghanistan.

title: Mahmud becomes ruler of Ghazni
description: Mahmud takes power in Ghazni and makes it the capital of an empire reaching from Iran to northern India.

title: Minaret of Jam built
description: The Ghurid sultan Ghiyath al-Din builds a 65-metre brick minaret in the mountains of Ghor, at the height of his dynasty's power.

title: Battle of Parwan
description: Jalal al-Din of Khwarazm defeats a Mongol army, after which Genghis Khan marches in person and lays waste to the cities of the region.

title: Herat becomes the Timurid capital
description: Shah Rukh succeeds his father Timur and rules from Herat, which becomes a centre of Persian art and learning.

title: Babur takes Kabul
description: Babur captures Kabul and makes it the base from which he later invades India and founds the Mughal Empire.

title: Mirwais Hotak's revolt
description: Mirwais Hotak kills the Safavid governor of Kandahar and founds the Hotak dynasty, the first independent Afghan state of the Ghilji Pashtuns.

title: Ahmad Shah Durrani chosen as king
description: An assembly of Pashtun chiefs elects Ahmad Shah as king, the founding of the Durrani Empire and of the modern Afghan state.

title: Capital moved to Kabul
description: Timur Shah Durrani moves the capital from Kandahar to Kabul.

title: Retreat from Kabul
description: A British and Indian army leaving Kabul is destroyed in the passes on the road to Jalalabad, the disaster of the First Anglo-Afghan War.

title: Treaty of Gandamak
description: After the first phase of the Second Anglo-Afghan War the amir Yaqub Khan gives Britain control of Afghanistan's foreign relations.

title: Battle of Maiwand
description: Ayub Khan's Afghan army defeats a British brigade west of Kandahar, one of the few British defeats of the war.

title: Abdur Rahman Khan becomes amir
description: Britain recognises Abdur Rahman Khan as amir, and over two decades he imposes central rule on the whole country.

title: Treaty of Rawalpindi
description: After the Third Anglo-Afghan War Britain recognises Afghanistan's full independence, including control of its foreign affairs.

title: Amanullah Khan abdicates
description: A tribal revolt against his rapid reforms forces the modernising king to give up the throne, and Kabul falls to the rebel Habibullah Kalakani.

title: Zahir Shah becomes king
description: Mohammed Zahir Shah succeeds his assassinated father Nadir Shah and reigns for forty years.

title: Constitution of 1964
description: Zahir Shah signs a constitution that creates an elected parliament and bars the royal family from government.

title: Daoud Khan's coup
description: Mohammed Daoud Khan overthrows his cousin Zahir Shah without bloodshed and declares a republic, ending the monarchy.

title: Saur Revolution
description: Army officers of the communist People's Democratic Party kill Daoud Khan and take power, beginning more than four decades of war.

title: Last Soviet troops leave
description: The last Soviet column crosses the Friendship Bridge over the Amu Darya, ending a nine-year occupation.

title: Mujahideen take Kabul
description: President Najibullah's government collapses and rival mujahideen groups enter the capital, which they then fight over for four years.

title: Taliban take Kabul
description: The Taliban capture the capital, kill former president Najibullah and proclaim the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.

title: Buddhas of Bamiyan destroyed
description: The Taliban blow up the two giant Buddhas as idols, despite international appeals.

title: United States invasion begins
description: The United States and Britain begin air strikes after the Taliban refuse to hand over Osama bin Laden, and the Taliban government falls within weeks.

title: Bonn Agreement
description: Afghan factions meeting under United Nations auspices agree on an interim government led by Hamid Karzai.

title: First direct presidential election
description: Hamid Karzai wins the first direct presidential election, held under the constitution adopted in January.

title: NATO ends its combat mission
description: The International Security Assistance Force is formally closed after thirteen years and Afghan forces take over the fighting against the Taliban.
